description.narrative: The Health Sector Development Program (the HSDP), consisting of a program grant for policy reforms and an accompanying project grant, will support the Government's 7th Health Sector Development Plan, 2011-2015, to improve primary health care (PHC) to achieve the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). This first-time program support to Lao PDR's health sector will help the Ministry of Health move toward a sector program approach. The combined outputs are (i) strengthened planning and financing; (ii) increased access to maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) care; and (iii) improved quality of human resources for health (HRH).

The number of poor and women accessing health equity funds increased by 10% each year. Progress/Status: Achieved 2010 and 2011: Project quarterly report 13. 2012, 2013, and 2014, “HEF Assessment Report, January 2015”. Based on number of HEF patient-visits 2010 - 12449 2011 - 23859 2012 - 23370 2013 - 37621 2014 - 47893 If we look at coverage, HEF coverage increased significantly with the addition of five provinces which increased eligible beneficiaries from about 100,000 in the first year to more than 430,000 at the end of the third year of the assessment period. HEF systems in the eight provinces are gender neutral, both for overall patient visits and for patient visits to each level of health care provider. Over the 3 year period (2012-2013) during which HEF has been active in 8 northern provinces, the total number of patient-visits has been 109,000 and the total number of female patient-visits has been 58,000 (53%). “HEF Assessment Report, January 2015”. Output: 2. Increased access to MNCH care. Indicator: 2.1. District hospitals meeting 75% of MNCH standards (BemONC services) increased by 5% each year. Progress/Status: Achieved Despite there is not baseline, the high cumulative achievement at 95% and specific project interventions in term of procurement of equipment for Bemonc and training of obstetric staff in Bemonc in 42 district hospitals allows to state the indicator has been achieved. A health facility data collection was carried out in August 2014 and assessed availability of Bemonc functions in all district hospitals and Cemonc functions in district hospitals type A. The results are as follow: Among 59 district hospitals in the northern region, 21 provide 7 functions, 27 provide 6 functions, and 8 provide 5 functions. It is a total of 56 district hospitals or 95%. Only 3 district hospitals provide less than 5 functions. Globally in all facilities in 8 northern provinces, between 2011 and 2014, the number of ANC, deliveries, and cesareans increased respectively by 80%, 50%, and 137%.
Data Source: Project household surveys, DPF, MOH

Provincial annual operational plans and budgets are results-based, realistic, and largely implemented as planned by December 2013. Output: 1. Strengthened planning and financing capacity. Indicator: 1.2. Measurable annual improvement of operations and maintenance of district hospitals and health centers between 2010 and 2014. Progress/Status: Achieved From 2010 to 2014, government budget allocated to operation has significantly increased as well as budget for maintenance of facilities and equipment. For example, in 2013-2014, about 2.4 million US$ have been allocated to health facilities in 8 northern provinces for non wage recurrent costs. This allocation supports operations and maintenance of health facilities and includes activities such as incentive for staff posted in remote facilities; small maintenance of facilities, equipment, vehicles; office and cleaning supplies; gasoline, communication (telephone, internet); regular meeting between eh different level of the health service (province, district, health center); regular supervision of district, health center and village level; short refresher training and on the job training; supply of drugs for village level; funding of HEF, free delivery, and development of model healthy villages; etc. This results in improvement of quality of services with increased utilization of facilities. Between 2011 and 2014: The number of OPD and IPD visits increased respectively by 89% and 52%. The number of deliveries in health facilities increased by 50%. The number of surgery procedures by 23%, and the number of cesarean sections by 137%. (source HMIS)
From 2010 to 2014, Government budget allocation for operations and maintenance of health facilities and equipment have been increased. For example, in FY2013-2014, about $2.03 million have been allocated to health facilities nationwide for non-wage recurrent costs. Data Source: Report of DPF, MOH

Output: 2. Increased access to MNCH care. Indicator: 2.2. Health facilities with sufficient amenities for privacy needs of women (delivery rooms, separate toilets and bathing rooms for women and men) increased by 5% each year. Progress/Status: Partially achieved There is no baseline and no annual facility survey to allow measurement of annual increase. The health facility data collection 2014 assesses amenities for privacy needs and results are as follow in district hospitals and health centers: 58/59 district hospitals have a delivery room (98%) 50/59 have functioning toilets in OPD area (85%) 37/59 have at least 2 toilets in OPD area (63%) 15/59 a sign showing males and females toilets (25%). Finally, 15/59 (25%) have both a delivery room and a sign showing males and females toilets.
286/414 health centers have a delivery room (69%) 330/414 have functioning toilets (80%) 90/414 have at least 2 toilets (22%) 39/414 a sign showing males and females toilets (9%). Finally, 38/414 (9%) have both a delivery room and a sign showing males and females toilets. For new facilities constructed, all specifications have adequate privacy- ADB models and JICA model reviewed in Checklist. Privacy facilities include separate toilets for male and female, toilet and shower near delivery room,; partitions between pairs of beds; high windows for delivery and MNCH room, for examination rooms (Report International Gender Consultant, Annex 2G).

Output: 3. Improved quality of HRH. Indicator: 3.4. University and college master plans are approved by 2013, with affirmative actions for females and ethnic groups. Progress/Status: Achieved The University of Health Sciences (UHS) developed and the MOH endorsed the UHS 5-year strategic development plan. The strategic plan is based on the Health Personnel Development Strategy (HPDS) by-2020 that includes actions to target improved educational attainment of female and ethnic group students, promotion of gender and ethnic equity and equal opportunities among health workers. It is the third pillar of the Health Personnel Development Strategy (HPDS) by-2020. The Health Personnel Information database has been developed and made operational. Annual report are produced to monitor implementation of the HPDS by 2020 and particularly indicators 3.2 & 3.2 with regard to ethnic groups and females in the health workforce.
